behavior: A block whose leading is tight against its glyph height is REFUSED rather than converted with a line lost, over the whole tight range, by two mechanisms behind one guarantee. This spec's trim guard refuses 12 pt on 9 pt (0.75 em) and 9 pt on 7 pt (0.78 em); CORE-006's consequence check refuses every tighter leading whose redaction would cost a neighbouring line its characters. 0.45, 0.60 and 0.70 em used to convert and lose two lines SILENTLY -- the second signer's reproduction, recorded in verification.md -- and they now refuse, naming the page and the object. At 0.83 em and above nothing is lost and the conversion proceeds. The identification defect that made the tight leadings lose lines is CORE-004 (#201), closed by verifying the consequence instead of repairing the identification; that mechanism is specified at `specs/archive/CORE-006-verify-by-consequence/`.

behavior: A large text object drawn under the text — a watermark, a stamp — does not change whether the page converts, whichever order it appears in. The object being replaced is the span whose bbox best matches the rect, not the first span whose bbox happens to contain the rect's centre: a 60 pt watermark satisfies the latter everywhere it crosses a line, became "the object being replaced", and made every trim impossible, so a page that had converted stopped converting. Span order decided the outcome, which is the second signer's first Major.
